### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Alsahan-Harris syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:21485)

**Proposed mechanism:** TBC1D32 (HGNC:21485) —DISRUPTS→ Disruption of TBC1D32 function (HP:0011220); Disruption of TBC1D32 function (HP:0011220) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal cellular trafficking (GO:0007010); Abnormal cellular trafficking (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Phenotype of MONDO:0009795 (HP:0000001); Abnormal cellular trafficking (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Phenotype of Alsahan-Harris syndrome (HP:0000002). Loss-of-function mutations in TBC1D32 lead to abnormal cellular trafficking, which in turn manifests as the distinct phenotypes of MONDO:0009795 and Alsahan-Harris syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in TBC1D32 with frequencies exceeding 1% in gnomAD across all populations would refute the hypothesis that these variants are the primary cause of either disease. _(variant: HGNC:21485)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TBC1D32 in both diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies that address the underlying cellular trafficking defects, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.

#### 2. retinitis pigmentosa 100  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.781)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:21485)

**Proposed mechanism:** TBC1D32 (HGNC:21485) —DISRUPTS→ Endosomal sorting and trafficking (GO:0006898); Endosomal sorting and trafficking (GO:0006898) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000511); Endosomal sorting and trafficking (GO:0006898) —LEADS_TO→ Nephronophthisis (HP:0000017). Loss-of-function mutations in TBC1D32 disrupt endosomal sorting and trafficking, leading to retinal degeneration in MONDO:0009795 and nephronophthisis-like symptoms (which can include retinal degeneration as a component phenotype) in retinitis pigmentosa 100 (MONDO:0979574).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in TBC1D32 that lead to gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if MONDO:0009795 and retinitis pigmentosa 100 were found to be caused by mutations in entirely distinct pathways that do not converge on endosomal trafficking, this would also falsify the hypothesis. _(variant: Presence of common benign variants in TBC1D32 in gnomAD that are inconsistent with a loss-of-function mechanism for both diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TBC1D32 in endosomal trafficking offers a potential therapeutic target for both MONDO:0009795 and retinitis pigmentosa 100, suggesting that interventions aimed at restoring or modulating endosomal function could benefit patients with either condition.
